newsitem.title: FRANCE: French farm machinery makers optimistic for 96.
newsitem.headline: French farm machinery makers optimistic for 96.

text.p: The year 1996 is shaping up as a good year for French farm machinery makers, whose sales jumped 13 percent in the first half, manufacturers' union SYGMA predicted on Friday.
But demand for farm machinery may stabilise in the first half of 1997, possibly slightly declining in full year 1997, it said.

In a statement SYGMA explained that cattle producers hard hit by the "mad cow" crisis limited or delayed investment plans this year and that uncertainty remained over their investment plans for next year.
But investment from grain producers, which harvested a bumper crop this year, should remain sustained.
Sales of French farm machinery rose to 11.3 billion francs in the first half of 1996 from 10 billion francs in the comparable period for 1995, mostly helped by higher farmers' income.
Sales had reached 15.2 billion francs in full year 1995, up 19 percent over 1994.
At end October French tractor registrations reached 27,973 units, up 15.3 percent over a year ago.
SYGMA predicted 36,000 new tractors may be registered in France in full year 1996 against 32,235 in 1995.
